concerns: Manufacturability & yield: Proposed bounded/enriched fractions must be produced at sufficient yield from conditioned medium to supply multiple in vivo arms and analytical controls; low yields will limit replicates and comparability testing (evidence: ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi supports source‑cell scalability concerns).

Process sensitivity & membrane integrity: Fractionation, concentration, and formulation steps can disrupt membranes or change capture epitope availability, confounding the qualitative gate; detergent/protease controls must be implemented and their impact on downstream assays characterized (evidence: ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Measurement feasibility: Recovering orthogonally verifiable intact EVs from low‑biomass matrices (nasal lavage, CSF, olfactory mucosa) is technically challenging; NTA/TRPS particle counts, capture ELISAs, and spike‑in recovery require validated LOD/LOQ for these matrices and potential interference from mucins and secretome (evidence: ev-misev2023-quality-framework; ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution highlights low detectability in large animal lavage/CSF).

Spike‑in tracer risk: The spike‑in must faithfully mimic endogenous EV capture and protection; if tracer behavior diverges, negative recovery could be misinterpreted as delivery failure or, conversely, false assurance (evidence: ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Lot comparability: The proposed qualitative gate is non‑numeric; without robust process controls and reproducible analytic recovery metrics, pass/fail decisions across lots may be inconsistent. Comparative studies across multiple conditioned‑medium lots and passage ranges are needed (evidence: ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi).

Stability & storage: Stability of the intact‑EV signature through sample handling, storage, and transport (including spike‑in stability) is not addressed and can affect both measurement and biological readouts; stability-indicating studies are required (evidence: ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Scale‑up risk: Manufacturing scale‑up may alter particle:protein ratios, membrane integrity, and capture epitope presentation; these attributes are central to the proposed gate but are sensitive to upstream process changes (evidence: ev-hermann-2023-neonatal-hi; ev-misev2023-quality-framework).

Translational/delivery uncertainty: Non‑human primate intranasal biodistribution was poor for reporter‑labeled EVs (strong nasal retention, negligible brain/CSF signal), creating a realistic risk that rodent in vivo→ex vivo linkage will not translate and limiting the QA relevance of the proposed attribute without a larger‑animal bridging strategy (evidence: ev-driedonks-2022-macaque-biodistribution).
conclusion: The proposal is conceptually supported by rodent intranasal efficacy reports and MISEV2023 guidance on orthogonal EV characterization, but it faces high manufacturability, measurement, and scale‑up risks that must be de‑risked before the attribute can be treated as a program gating quality attribute. Priorities: (1) invest in analytical sensitivity/orthogonal capture and spike‑in tracer qualification before in vivo bridging; (2) confirm achievable yields and membrane‑integrity retention across the proposed fractionation and handling steps (including detergent/protease controls) to enable lot comparability; and (3) plan an early larger‑animal pilot or bridging assessment to address species/delivery uncertainty highlighted by macaque data. Only if analytical recovery, reproducible short‑interval in vivo exposure, and processly robust retention of the intact‑EV signature are demonstrated should the proposed qualitative intact‑EV gate be adopted for CMC decisions.
evidence_gap: Critical experimental and analytical gaps: validated spike‑in tracer characterization showing parity with endogenous EV capture/protection behavior; quantitative limits-of-detection and recovery for capture from low‑biomass nasal lavage/CSF after proposed fractionation; yield and membrane‑integrity retention data across the intended preparative workflow (SEC/iodixanol, concentration steps, buffers) to support lot comparability and scale‑up; and a small large‑animal (or orthogonally justified) delivery assessment to address the macaque negative biodistribution signal.
